title: Inline-Six Marine Diesel
subtitle: Six cylinders, one crankshaft and a turbocharger that feeds them compressed air
summary: A marine diesel turns heavy fuel into shaft power for a ship. Air is compressed by the turbocharger, cooled, and forced into six cylinders; fuel is injected at the top of each compression stroke and ignites without a spark. The pistons push connecting rods, the rods turn the crankshaft, and the flywheel smooths the pulses into steady rotation.

parts.name: Bedplate and Mounts
parts.short: The foundation that carries the engine
parts.detail: A rigid cast bedplate spreads the engine's weight and firing loads into the ship's hull. Flexible mounts isolate vibration from the structure.

parts.name: Crankcase
parts.short: Houses the crankshaft and oil
parts.detail: The crankcase surrounds the rotating crankshaft and forms the oil sump. Inspection doors let engineers check bearings without lifting the engine.

parts.name: Cylinder Block
parts.short: The water-jacketed body of the engine
parts.detail: A single casting that carries the six liners, the camshaft and the cylinder heads. Coolant passages are cast into its walls.

parts.name: Cylinder Liners
parts.short: Replaceable bores the pistons run in
parts.detail: Hardened wet liners sit in the block and are cooled by water on their outside. They can be renewed without replacing the whole block.

parts.name: Pistons
parts.short: Six pistons that turn pressure into force
parts.detail: Each piston takes the push of combustion and passes it to a connecting rod. Rings seal the bore and carry heat into the liner.

parts.name: Connecting Rods
parts.short: Link each piston to the crankshaft
parts.detail: The rod's small end follows the piston while its big end circles the crank pin. It converts straight-line force into rotation.

parts.name: Crankshaft and Flywheel
parts.short: Collects all six power strokes
parts.detail: Offset crank pins turn the rods' push into torque. The heavy flywheel stores energy between firing strokes and smooths the drive.

parts.name: Cylinder Heads
parts.short: Close the cylinders and hold the valves
parts.detail: Each head carries intake and exhaust valves, springs and the injector. It seals the combustion chamber against enormous pressure.

parts.name: Camshaft and Rockers
parts.short: Open the valves at the right moment
parts.detail: The camshaft's lobes push pushrods, which rock the arms that open the valves. Its half-speed drive is timed to the crankshaft.

parts.name: Fuel Injectors
parts.short: Spray fuel into each cylinder
parts.detail: The injector atomises fuel at the end of compression, when the air is hot enough to ignite it without a spark.

parts.name: Fuel Pump and Governor
parts.short: Meters fuel and holds engine speed
parts.detail: The injection pump times each pulse, while the governor adjusts fuel delivery to keep the requested speed as load changes.

parts.name: Intake Manifold
parts.short: Distributes charge air to the cylinders
parts.detail: A common rail feeds cooled, compressed air to each intake port. Even distribution matters for balanced cylinder temperatures.

parts.name: Exhaust Manifold
parts.short: Collects hot gas for the turbine
parts.detail: The manifold joins all six exhaust ports into one hot stream that drives the turbocharger's turbine wheel.

parts.name: Turbocharger
parts.short: Uses exhaust gas to compress intake air
parts.detail: Exhaust spins the turbine wheel, which turns the compressor wheel on the same shaft. More air means more fuel can be burned.

parts.name: Air Filter
parts.short: Cleans air before the compressor
parts.detail: A pleated element traps dust and salt before it reaches the compressor, where it would erode the blades.

parts.name: Charge-Air Cooler
parts.short: Cools compressed air before the engine
parts.detail: Compression heats the air; cooling it makes it denser, so each cylinder can take in more oxygen.

parts.name: Starter Motor
parts.short: Turns the engine for the first firing
parts.detail: A geared electric motor spins the flywheel until compression and fuel produce the first power strokes.

parts.name: Lube Oil Pump
parts.short: Pressurises oil for bearings
parts.detail: The pump pushes oil through a filter and gallery to every bearing. Loss of pressure stops the engine within seconds.

parts.name: Seawater Pump
parts.short: Supplies raw water for cooling
parts.detail: The pump moves seawater through the heat exchanger, where it takes heat from the engine's closed coolant loop.

parts.name: Heat Exchanger
parts.short: Transfers engine heat to seawater
parts.detail: A bundle of tubes keeps coolant and seawater apart while letting heat pass from one to the other.

parts.name: Nameplate
parts.short: Model, rating and serial number
parts.detail: The plate records the engine's continuous rating and serial number for service and spare parts.

steps.title: Air first
steps.body: The turbocharger compresses intake air and the charge cooler removes the heat of compression. Dense air lets each cylinder burn more fuel in the same volume.

steps.title: Compression ignites the fuel
steps.body: The piston rises and squeezes air to a high pressure and temperature. The injector sprays fuel into that hot air; it ignites without a spark.

steps.title: Rods turn push into rotation
steps.body: Combustion drives each piston down. The connecting rod follows the crank pin and turns the crankshaft, while the flywheel carries the engine through the next compression stroke.

steps.title: Heat must leave the engine
steps.body: Coolant circulates through the block and head, then gives its heat to seawater in the heat exchanger. Oil carries heat away from bearings at the same time.

quiz.prompt: Tap the part that collects all six power strokes into rotation.
Tap the part that uses exhaust gas to compress intake air.
Tap the part that sprays fuel into the cylinder.
Why is the charge-air cooler used?
quiz.explain: Cooling compressed air reduces its volume, so more oxygen enters each cylinder.

quiz.prompt: What drives the turbocharger's compressor wheel?
choices: Exhaust gas turning the turbine wheel
quiz.explain: The turbine and compressor share a shaft; exhaust gas spins the turbine and therefore the compressor.
